articles.summary: Toronto and most of southern Ontario has been enjoying warmer temperatures but it’s approaching that time of year when you need to start making the switch to winter tires. articles.title: Woman dead, man arrested after stabbing in North York: Toronto police
articles.summary: Toronto police are investigating a homicide after a woman died in a stabbing in North York Friday morning.

articles.title: Female fatally stabbed in North York; male in custody, police say
articles.summary: The Toronto Police Service (TPS) has launched a homicide investigation after a female was fatally stabbed in North York on Friday morning. Investigators were called to the Wilson Avenue and Jane Street area for reports of a person with a knife just before 8:30 a.m. on Nov. 6. A female was located with stab wounds. […]

articles.title: OPP and Hamilton police team up to dismantle auto theft network
articles.summary: Six people are facing charges after an investigation into an organized group that was allegedly stealing high-value vehicles throughout southwestern Ontario. The Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) and Hamilton Police Service (HPS) both launched separate probes into the group in February, 2026. Later realizing that their investigations were connected, they teamed up to form Project TORRENS […]

articles.title: Mamdani and Hochul promise a new day for Puerto Rico after Democrats sweep midterms
articles.summary: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and New York Gov. Kathy Hochul pledged more support for Puerto Rico on Friday as it remains mired in multiple crises, asserting during a trip to the island that the sweeping Democratic win in the U.S. midterm elections will be a boon for the U.S. territory.

articles.title: City of Toronto pauses hiring, citing 'financial pressures' ahead of budget season
articles.summary: As Toronto stares down another difficult budget season, with a $1-billion shortfall, a hiring freeze is being put in place at city hall. The pause won't apply to emergency services, but means some job applications have been paused partway through the process.

articles.title: U of T dean of dentistry steps down after investigation into antisemitic images in course material
articles.summary: The University of Toronto says its dean of dentistry Anil Kishen voluntarily stepped down following an investigation into his use of antisemitic imagery in February.

articles.title: 2 women, 2 children, struck by vehicle in Richmond Hill, Ont.: police
articles.summary: York Regional Police say four pedestrians, including two children, were struck by a vehicle in Richmond Hill, north of Toronto, on Thursday afternoon.

articles.title: Toronto fire chief welcomes new lithium-ion regulations in record-setting year for battery fires
articles.summary: Toronto's fire chief says new regulations from Queen's Park to ban people from modifying lithium-ion batteries are a welcome "first step." The city has already seen more than 120 blazes sparked by the batteries this year alone.

articles.title: Victim in fatal North York stabbing identified: police
articles.summary: A woman who was fatally stabbed in an incident that left two people dead has been identified by Toronto police.

articles.title: 2 arrested, police searching for suspect after Mississauga apartment building allegedly set on fire twice
articles.summary: Two people have been arrested and police are searching for a third in connection with two fires they allege were deliberately set in September at a Mississauga apartment building.

articles.title: U.S.-made pipes are being installed next to Ontario's legislature as Canadian steel jobs vanish
articles.summary: As Canadian governments push to improve local supply chains amidst an ongoing trade war with the United States, the City of Toronto has been forced to head south of the border. Officials say only American companies make the steel pipes they are currently installing near Queen's Park.
